subject: Unexpected overage from adaptive thresholding — request for breakdown and VAT treatment
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@lumenpay.co.uk>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: Accounts Payable <ap@lumenpay.co.uk>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Unexpected May overage — need breakdown and VAT treatment

Hi Chloe,

Hope you're well. We received invoice INV-1298 for May and there is an unexpected ~48% overage compared to our forecast. Line item shows this as 'adaptive-threshold premium'. We don't have a clear mapping of which requests pushed into the adaptive threshold vs normal metering.

Could you provide:
- Per-route token counts (chat.generate / embeddings) for 2026-05-01 -> 2026-05-31
- A short explanation of why the adaptive threshold applied (trigger criteria) and which requests were affected
- Confirmation of VAT treatment for the overage (we are an EU entity, want to understand reverse-charge vs Redwood charging VAT)

We need this to clear the invoice with our AP team by next week. I've attached the invoice we received.

Thanks,
Aisha
Billing & Ops
LumenPay Ltd.

Attachment: invoice_INV-1298-202605.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

Ben / Marissa — can you take point on this? LumenPay's AP needs per-route counts + an explanation of the adaptive threshold behavior. I started a quick look and it looks like their traffic pattern hit the new adaptive-rate bucket on May 18 after a cadence change.

A few notes I pulled:
- They use both chat.generate and embeddings in production; embeddings spikes on 2026-05-18 coincided with a model variant fallback that increased token expansion.
- Ben, can you pull per-route token sampling and the sampling_evidence CSV? Marissa, please confirm VAT treatment and whether we applied EU VAT on the invoice or reversed charged.

I'll keep LumenPay on the thread for questions.

—Chloe
Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Cc: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:26:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected May overage — per-route counts and sampling evidence

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for flagging this — I've attached a CSV extract (sampling_evidence_202605.csv) with per-route token tallies and a short root-cause summary below.

Summary (short):
- On 2026-05-18 03:40 UTC LumenPay's production worker pool performed a large batch of backfill embedding calls while switching to the new 'gpt-3.8-embed-q' quantized variant. The quantized variant increased average token expansion for a subset of batched requests by ~1.9x vs their baseline.
- Redwood's adaptive thresholding rule (enabled in their account on 2026-04-30) changes the metering bucket when a sequence of requests exceeds 3x baseline tokens over a rolling 30-minute window. The backfill pattern triggered the adaptive premium tier for ~6 hours that day.
- The invoice shows the premium multiplier applied only to tokens flagged by the thresholding rule. The attached CSV flags each session id and the meter decision we recorded.

VAT: Marissa will confirm the tax treatment, but per our records we did NOT charge VAT on INV-1298 (we applied reverse-charge on EU entity LumenPay Ltd.). I'll let Marissa confirm and attach the tax note.

Next steps:
1) I attached sampling_evidence_202605.csv with per-route counts and trigger markers.
2) Chloe / Marissa: recommend we offer one-time good-faith offset for the portion attributable to the quantized-model fallback (customer-facing explanation + 25% credit on the premium lines) while we review telemetry. Is that OK?

Ben Carter
Account Executive (Renewals)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sampling_evidence_202605.csv

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@lumenpay.co.uk>, Accounts Payable <ap@lumenpay.co.uk>
Cc: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected May overage — VAT and collection options

Hi Aisha,

Confirming VAT treatment: Redwood has applied reverse-charge for LumenPay Ltd. on INV-1298 (we have LumenPay's EU VAT id on file). That means we did not add UK/EU VAT to the invoice total. I've attached a short tax note to the Drive link (included below) and can provide a PDF in case your AP needs a stamped tax note.

On the overage itself: we reviewed the sampling evidence Ben provided. Given the fallback / quantized-variant expansion appears to be the primary driver, we are prepared to apply a one-time 25% credit to the premium portion (line items flagged 'adaptive-threshold') to help bridge your AP hold. The credit will be applied as a post-invoice adjustment appearing as CR-1298 on your next statement.

If you'd prefer immediate netting so you can release payment for the remainder, we can:
- Issue CR-1298 now (reduces outstanding balance) and apply a 30-day term for the remaining amount, or
- Leave invoice as-is and apply the credit to next invoice cycle (no change to payment due now).

Let us know which you prefer and we will route to collections.

Marissa Cole
Billing Lead
Redwood Inference

Related link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d5e

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. We appreciate the sampling CSV and the proposed credit. LumenPay's AP would like the credit issued now so we can pay the net amount and close the month. Please issue CR-1298 and send an updated invoice reflecting the net due. Once we receive the adjusted invoice we'll process payment under our standard 30-day terms.

Tom Reynolds

LumenPay Ltd.
